title: Moorabool River basin (Victoria, Australia) - FS28 nature-based-solutions feasibility study
status: worked example - NOT a set of defaults
how_to_read: This is one project's fully parameterised InVEST tables, kept so the model can see how a real study chose and justified every coefficient. Numbers are specific to a temperate, winter-wet, Mediterranean-type SE Australian catchment on a 19-class local land-cover legend. Reuse a value ONLY after checking its 'context' and the matching record in the per-parameter files; prefer re-deriving from those.

study_context.region: Moorabool River basin, Victoria, Australia (Corangamite CMA; basin no. 232)
study_context.climate: temperate oceanic / Mediterranean-type; cool wet season May-Oct generates most runoff; warm dry summer
study_context.note: The FS28 file does not include Carbon, AWY root_depth or AWY/SWY as run models; its hydrology was done in eWater Source, not InVEST SWY. The CN and Kc tables here are still directly usable for InVEST SWY.
study_context.land_cover_legend: Victoria DEECA Land Cover Time Series (25 m, 1987-2019), 19 classes; land use from VLUIS 2023-2024
scenarios: all optionally under CMIP6 SSP2-4.5 climate change

dem.dataset: GEDTM30 (~30 m global DTM, ML fusion of ICESat-2 + GEDI)

rainfall_erosivity_R.dataset: Teng et al. 2016 Australia, ~1 km, TRMM-based (Renard & Freimund 1994)

soil_erodibility_K.dataset: Teng et al. 2016 Australia, ~1 km, vis-NIR spectroscopy + Cubist

raster_inputs.climate_station_access: BoM Climate Data Online (p_nccObsCode 136 rain, 122/123 tmax/tmin, 193/194 sunshine/solar); Victoria WMIS for streamflow
raster_inputs.beneficiaries: WorldPop 2020 Australia population density, accumulated downstream per sub-basin

legend_crosswalk.note: DEECA class -> the simplified 'homologated' class the coefficient tables were keyed on (approx. ESA WorldCover-compatible)

biophysical_table.bmp_rows_note: Codes 21 (Crop Area BMPs - Dryland), 22 (Crop Area BMPs - Horticulture), 23 (Livestock Area BMPs) are management scenarios on the SAME land use: usle_c reduced 30% (crop) / 50% (livestock); load_n -25%, load_p -30% (crop), load_n -20%, load_p -50% (livestock); CN lowered 25 units (crop) / 18 units (livestock).
biophysical_table.known_inconsistency: The FS28 'BiophysicalTable' sheet and 'NDR params' assembled table disagree on proportion_subsurface_n (e.g. lucode 4: 0.77 vs 0.47) and on crit_len_p ordering. The values above follow the 'NDR params' assembled table (Raji et al. 2020-derived, standard InVEST semantics). Re-check against your own NDR run.

source_attribution.usle_c: mixed: Teng et al. 2016 (Australia), Yang et al. 2003, Bakker et al. 2008 - see usle_c.json
source_attribution.ndr_columns: Raji et al. 2020 (tropical semi-arid) mapped onto DEECA classes; Redhead et al. 2018 for the improved-grassland N/P loads; Ludemann et al. 2022 cross-check on Australian cropland
source_attribution.CN_A..D: Asante et al. 2008 (GeoSFM) for most classes; Jaafar et al. 2019 (GCN250) for disturbed ground, hardwood & conifer plantations, good-condition native grassland & scattered trees
source_attribution.kc_annual_mean: FAO-56 (Allen et al. 1998) applied to Copernicus 300 m LAI time series 2023-2024, k=0.5, cap 1.2

kc_monthly.note: monthly Kc (Jan..Dec) per DEECA class, from the FS28 'Kc' sheet second block. Use for InVEST SWY Kc_1..Kc_12.

nbs_maturation.note: For scenario timelines, not InVEST tables. Each NbS reaches full functional benefit on a sigmoid curve; parameters below from the FS28 'NbS' sheet (each with ~20 cited references).
